new.title: Deleting a lead technician leaves no Unknown Technician column in Board View
preconditions: You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.

Technician {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST SV11416 Dana Delete) is a new staff member made for this case only, active at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and the Technician role, with no labor recorded on any work order, because this test deletes them.
Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST SV11416 Deleted Lead") is used by this case only.
Approved work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17901) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A}.
On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Asset on Site shows no choice (if its chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip), Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
steps: Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Board View in the display switcher.
Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
Read the header of the column that holds {Work-order-1}.
Click your initials (top right) and open Settings > Staff.
Click Delete and confirm the deletion.
Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click List in the display switcher.
Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
Read the Lead Technician of {Work-order-1} and write it down.
Click Board View in the display switcher.
Find {Work-order-1} and read the header of the column that holds it.
results: Step 3: {Work-order-1} is in a column headed with {Technician-A}'s name.
Step 11: {Work-order-1} is not in a column headed "Unknown Technician". Every column header on the board names whose column it is.
Step 11: if {Work-order-1} is still in a technician's column, that column's header shows the same name as the Lead Technician you wrote down at step 9.
expect_fail: Known problem (SV-11416, open: https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-11416): today, at step 11, {Work-order-1} sits in a column headed "Unknown Technician" with a generic person icon. The deleted technician's name is not shown and the column has no inactive marker.
1. If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new.
2. If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it.
3. If it passes, the fix has shipped: tell the QA lead.
new.source: Epic SV-10043; story SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 58 (15 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S5-R11b and S3-R3, with S3-N2, S3-N4 and the Decisions entry of 2026-09-13 as the nearest rules, read 16 Oct 2026. Defect SV-11416 (open). Source-verified 16 October 2026.
new.divergence: The spec says what happens when a lead technician is deactivated (the work stays in their column, marked inactive, so it stays attributable) but not when the technician is deleted. SV-11416 asks the product owner to decide: show the technician's name with the inactive marker, as for a deactivated technician, or move the work order to Unassigned. Either keeps this case's results; once the product owner decides, this case is updated to that ruling.
quotes: Every technician name in Tech View and Board View, on cards, rows, group headers, column headers and the names shown on hover over any technician avatar (S2-R10, S7-R1), is the technician’s staff record name, the same name the List’s Lead Technician column shows.
Column headers (technician names and counts) stay pinned at the top of the board while the user scrolls vertically, so long columns never hide whose column is being viewed.
Keep matching work visible in its deactivated technician’s column.
Show an inactive indicator on deactivated technician columns.

Deactivating a technician does not change work orders they already lead. They remain the lead technician on those work orders so the work stays visible and attributable; they simply receive no new assignments (S2-N2, S3-N2, S3-E3).
new.checked: Last checked against staging on 10/16/2026: failed as described in SV-11416 (the ticket does not record the build marker).
doc_part1: Sign in as an Owner or Admin user. On a QA site click the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView". To check the permissions: your initials (top right) > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders: View and Create & Edit are on.

Pick one location for the whole case; it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (to change it: your initials > Change Location). This is {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). Create everything below at {Location-A}.
Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (narrower windows show only the List, with no display switcher).

Your initials > Settings > Staff > New Staff Member. Make a new one for this case, never reuse one, because the test deletes it. Enter First Name and Last Name (for example ZZAUTOTEST SV11416 Dana Delete), an Email with ZZAUTOTEST in it, Role Technician, at least one Department (required), Location {Location-A}, turn Time Clock on, then Save & Close. Make sure the staff member is active. Do not record labor for them on any work order. This is {Technician-A}.

Top menu Customers > New Customer > Name (for example "ZZAUTOTEST SV11416 Deleted Lead") > Save. This is {Customer-A}; use it for this case only. On the customer page click Contacts > New Contact > First Name and Last Name (for example ZZAUTOTEST Contact) > Save. Then Assets > New Asset > pick the contact, Year (for example 2022), Make (type "Freight" and pick Freightliner), Model (for example M2), Unit (for example TRK-118) > Save. Contact and Make are required.

Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick {Customer-A} and its asset > Save (if a Confirmation about the credit limit appears, click Create). The work order opens on its Lines tab with the New Line form. In What Are You Doing? type "grease" and pick the ready-made line "Service - Full grease service", turn Line Approved on and click Save & Close. The status reads Approved. Write down the number shown at the top left (for example S10043-17901). This is {Work-order-1}. On {Work-order-1}'s page pick {Technician-A} in the Lead Technician dropdown; it saves at once (the dropdown shows once the work order is Approved).
Work Orders > All: clear any Status selection, click the x on the Asset on Site chip if it shows Yes or No, turn Assigned to me off and empty Search.
Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All > Board View > Search the name of {Customer-A} shows {Work-order-1} in {Technician-A}'s column. Then empty Search.
doc_part2: Goal: delete the lead technician of one work order and read Board View's column header for that work order, then compare it with List's Lead Technician.

Fact (C368191 run, 15 Oct 2026, staging): deleting a staff member who has recorded labor is refused with "Staff is being used elsewhere." This case's technician has no labor, only the lead, so the delete goes through (SV-11416 steps).
The test deletes {Technician-A}, so each run needs a new technician; the old ZZAUTOTEST work order and customer can stay.
Evidence: a screenshot after each step that has an expected result, the build marker, and the real value of every brace name.
new.why: SV-11416 (QA lead, 16 Oct 2026): a deleted lead technician's work order shows under "Unknown Technician" in Board View.
